about: Overhangs and supports. Every printed part has one bed face (the face of its 3mf entries in fusion/parts.json): the part is checked turned with that face down. A downward face steeper than the limit needs a support and is a finding, unless it is a bridge short enough, rests on the bed, or is a heat-set pocket ceiling (the one allowed support, listed, not failed). A horizontal round hole is a finding of its own: it is a teardrop. Lengths mm, angles degrees. A project changes a number only in its gate/settings.json ("overhang": {...}, merged over this file). An overhang that is really needed passes only as a named exception of the project: gate/settings.json "overhang": {"exceptions": [{"part", "at": [x, y, z] world mm, or "face": index, "code" (optional), "reason": why it cannot be redesigned}]}; it is listed under "excepted", never silently. Owner 2026-11-24: overhangs only "якщо це прям дуже треба".

limit_deg.source: owner 2026-11-24: "45 degree rises"; fusion/DESIGN_RULES.md section 5 (planar 45 degree chamfers). Measured from the vertical: a face at 45 degrees passes, a 50 degree cone fails. The tolerance takes the facets of a tessellated curve

bridge_max_mm.source: fusion/DESIGN_RULES.md section 5: "Bridges <= 6 mm (for example M3 head channels)"

bridge_flat_deg.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: a ceiling within 1 degree of flat is printed as a bridge, steeper ones as an overhang

ledge_mm.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: a flat ceiling no further than this from an edge held from below is a ledge, not an overhang: the wall line (0.62 on the 0.6 nozzle, 0.42 on the 0.4) still sits on the layer below. Bambu Studio did not support the 0.38 mm ledges of J3 forearm link A and the 0.4 mm ones of the switch cradles

bed_mm.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: one first layer of the 0.6 nozzle projects (0.3); a downward face no higher than that above the bed prints on the bed

min_area_mm2.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: smaller downward patches (tooth-end corners, 0.3-0.8 mm2 ceilings) are counted per part, not listed; at 0.25 the gate and the independent mesh audit split on them by how each samples a sub-millimetre bridge

sliver_mm.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: a flat downward face whose mean width (2 x area / perimeter) is under this is a modelling sliver (two faces 0.05 mm apart), not an overhang: listed in info as sliver

grid_mm.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: the step of the points a flat ceiling is sampled at to find its bridged part

ridge_min_mm.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: a shallow ridge shorter than this is not listed

codes.overhang: downward face steeper than the limit, not a bridge: give it a 45 degree rise from below, or lay the part on another side
codes.round_hole: horizontal round hole: its top needs a support; give it a teardrop top (45 degree roof, flat top no wider than the bridge)
codes.long_bridge: flat ceiling held on both sides but longer than bridge_max_mm: narrow it, or a 45 degree roof
codes.shallow_ridge: two downward faces meet in an edge that rises less than the limit (fusion/DESIGN_RULES.md section 5: two 45 degree faces that slope different ways meet in a shallower edge): give the faces the same tilt so the ridge runs level, or 45 degrees along the ridge
codes.no_bed_face: the part has no bed face in fusion/parts.json (3mf entries with "face"): name the face it prints on
codes.bed_face_conflict: the part's 3mf entries name different bed faces: one part, one print orientation
codes.heatset_ceiling: ALLOWED: the ceiling of a heat-set pocket that opens sideways or downwards: the insert needs the round pocket, a support or a sacrificial layer is fine (owner 2026-11-24)
codes.exception_without_reason: a project exception in gate/settings.json covers this overhang but gives no reason: write why it is really needed, or redesign it
codes.exception_unused: a project exception in gate/settings.json matches no finding: remove it
codes.slicer_bridge: a flat ceiling the geometry passes as a bridge, but Bambu Studio puts support under it whatever the bridge settings (bridge_no_support, max_bridge_length: it does not take it for a bridge, e.g. a ceiling over tooth gaps open on one side): give it a 45 degree roof, close its open side with a wall, or lay the part on another side

slicer.source: gate author's choice 2026-11-24: support moves are binned in 1 mm cells; a support cell and a gate region match within 2 mm; a part with less than 20 mm of support line and no gate region agrees (the old support gate's noise floor: 20 mm); a bridge the gate allows with at least bridge_contact_mm2 of support contact on it (each contact cell counted once, for the nearest region, within one cell of its box) is the finding slicer_bridge: gate author's choice 2026-11-24, after a copy of robotarm-v2-04.3mf sliced with bridge_no_support = 1 kept the support under the 216T tooth-gap ceilings unchanged
